decisions.title: Acceptance criteria and definition-of-done stay advisory at task completion, but completion must report unresolved items
decisions.context: Opened by an inbound report from quest-web (via the orchestrator): a task with one unchecked acceptance criterion completed silently -- exit 0, no warning, nothing in the record. A second, independent incident on 2026-09-13 (another fleet session) closed two tasks with 0 of 3 criteria checked, via the older 1-based --check-ac numbering trap (QCLI-269) whose usage errors went unseen. QCLI-252's own investigation found zero enforcement anywhere in src/ tying acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone to the completion transition (only gates/gateEvents block, a structurally separate field), and confirmed command-help.ts and the task-finalization guide never said so plainly.
decisions.outcome: Kept advisory, but stopped being silent: quest task complete now computes an additive unresolvedAtCompletion field (acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone unchecked items, index+text) on its JSON result -- present only when something is unresolved, matching this codebase's omit-when-empty convention -- and prints a stderr line prefixed Warning: naming the unresolved items. Exit code and the completed record's own fields are unchanged; opum-cli-e2e's contract check.stderrSilentOnSuccess already tolerates a warning-prefixed line on success, so this does not read as a failure to any known consumer. command-help.ts's task complete summary and the task-finalization guide now state this plainly. Scoped to task complete only (not archive/pause/start/demote), since completion is the one transition where whether the work was actually finished is the live question.

decisions.title: migration_not_found reclassifies as error_type not_found; sibling migration lifecycle not-found paths move with it
decisions.context: QCLI-257: quest migration backlog status --digest <unknown> --json returned {"error_type":"validation","message":"migration_not_found"} on exit 6, not not_found on exit 3. Root cause: MigrationBacklogService.status() (src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts) throws a plain new Error("migration_not_found") instead of one of the typed domain errors src/cli/main.ts's top-level classifier recognizes; a plain Error whose message is not in its hardcoded not_found list (task_not_found, draft_not_found, milestone_not_found, decision_not_found) falls through to the validation default. rollback() calls status() internally, so it throws and misclassifies the identical message on the identical path -- one fix covers both. apply()'s own not-yet-approved-digest case is a different message, migration_approval_digest_mismatch, raised when a freshly recomputed preview digest does not match the caller-supplied one; that is a genuine input-validation mismatch against current source state; it is not a missing-record lookup, so it does not share this gap and is left classified as validation. Grounding: the shared Opum result contract (Ratify the Quest CLI result contract, QCLI-24/QCLI-69) reserves error_type not_found and exit 3 specifically for a read command's not-found outcome, distinct from validation on exit 6; the component contracts reference document states a read command's not-found outcome must be unambiguous and distinguished from an unrelated hard error.
decisions.outcome: Reclassified: migration_not_found is added to src/cli/main.ts's not_found message list alongside task_not_found/draft_not_found/milestone_not_found/decision_not_found, so quest migration backlog status and quest migration backlog rollback both report error_type: not_found on exit 3 for an unknown or never-previewed digest, matching the name and a caller's reasonable expectation, and matching the ADR's own not-found convention. quest migration backlog apply's migration_approval_digest_mismatch is left as error_type: validation on exit 6 -- it is a digest-mismatch-against-current-source-state validation, not an absent-record lookup, so it does not share the gap this decision addresses. A caller distinguishing the two: branch on error_type (not_found vs validation), not on message text -- message strings are diagnostic detail, not part of the classification contract.

decisions.title: task view / lore context: projection, enforced bounds, and reported omission are one shared shape across quest and lore (QCLI-276 / LCLI-478)
decisions.context:
Two independent gaps turned out to be one problem, surfaced the same night: LCLI-478 (lore-cli) found `lore context`'s maxTokens budget advisory -- a target could exceed it and the result was merely marked truncated, no separate exact-read path existed for proof evidence. QCLI-276 (this repo) found `task view` has no field or note projection and always returns the full record; a probe task's implementationNotes had already passed 1M characters. opum-agent (OPAG-142) ruled the two repos design one agreed shape together before either implements, rather than each inventing a reasonable-but-different answer that a consumer driving both products (mbpm2, concretely) would then have to learn twice.

Agreed between quest-cli and lore-cli sessions, cross-session, 2026-09-14. lore-cli's own side is now written: DEC-2 in lore-cli's own Quest workspace (PR #77), cross-linked here rather than duplicated. DEC-2 marks lore's three still-open specifics -- the hard-budget flag spelling, the exact-read operation's name, and the omission marker's spelling -- as pending design, not declined or deferred; LCLI-478 implementation has not started as of this update.
decisions.outcome:
Three SEMANTICS are shared across both repos; the flag spelling, unit, and granularity are NOT forced to match, because the underlying bounds are genuinely different kinds of thing, not the same bound in different units:

1. PROJECTION is additive and opt-in. A consumer names what it wants; absent means everything, so today's default output is byte-for-byte unchanged on both sides. quest's default `task view <id>` stays the full unbounded record -- there is no separately-named "exact read" operation the way lore needs one, because projection is purely additive on top of an unchanged default.

2. A SUPPLIED BOUND IS ENFORCED, NOT ADVISORY. If a caller supplies one, the response never silently exceeds it. This is the piece both sides hold hardest: an advisory budget is the same silence-parses-as-optional failure this release (0.7.0) exists to close, in a different costume -- a caller asks for a guarantee and gets a suggestion, with no way to tell which one it received.

3. OMISSION IS ALWAYS REPORTED WHEN PROJECTION IS ACTIVE, NEVER INFERRED FROM A COUNT. Whatever a bounded response drops, it says so explicitly, and the marker is present whenever a projection flag was supplied -- including the zero case (nothing was actually omitted) -- not only when something was. An absent marker is ambiguous between "nothing omitted" and "a caller too old to report it"; present-and-zero is unambiguous and costs one integer. (The marker is correctly absent when NO projection flag is given at all -- full record, nothing to report.) A consumer must never have to diff against a full fetch to discover a partial one.

UNITS AND GRANULARITY DIFFER BY DESIGN, STATED HERE SO IT READS AS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN INCONSISTENCY: lore bounds by TOKENS across an assembled context pack (a whole-pack budget) because `lore context` assembles an LLM-context pack where token budget is the real constraint and the assembly is lossy by design (selection, ordering, truncation). quest bounds by RECORD COUNT on a single field (a per-field cap: `--max-notes N` on `task view`), because quest is a plain JSON record store with no token-shaped concern and its default is already an exact, unassembled read -- the actual unbounded-growth fields are `implementationNotes` and `comments` arrays, not the record as a whole. These are different KINDS of bound, not the same bound in different units; a consumer working across both products should expect the three semantics above to hold, and should read each tool's own flag list for the specifics, not assume the spelling transfers.

quest-side concrete shape for QCLI-276: `task view` gains `--max-notes N` (and optionally `--since <ISO date>`), additive/opt-in, default unchanged. Whenever any projection flag is supplied, the response carries a `notesOmitted: <count>` sibling field next to `implementationNotes` (0 when nothing was capped, the real count otherwise) -- present whenever projection was requested, never only-when-nonzero. A general `--fields a,b,c` selector for the rest of the record may follow later if a concrete pain point appears; none exists today the way it does for notes.

lore-side concrete shape for LCLI-478: an unbudgeted exact-read operation exists as a SEPARATE named operation, not a flag on the assembling default (structural, since `lore context`'s default is lossy by design, unlike quest's) -- otherwise the same three semantics, its own flag spelling and token-based unit. Full detail in lore-cli's own record, cross-linked once it lands.

Neither QCLI-276 nor LCLI-478 dispatches to an implementer until both sides confirm this record matches their own understanding.

decisions.title: QCLI-284: version-only stays exit 0 by design; the embedded CI-hint sentence was the thing that lied, not the exit code
decisions.context: lore-cli reported that its CLAUDE.md carried a stale Quest CLI version across two minor releases undetected, because CI's quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude reported exit 0 (state: version-only) the whole time, while the managed block's own generated text read: current instructions exit 0, while missing, drifted, or malformed managed instructions exit 6. That sentence names three failure categories and omits version-only entirely, so a reader concludes CI catches version drift via the exit-6 promise when by design it does not. Two candidate fixes, with different blast radii, were named up front rather than picked blind: (a) the exit code is wrong -- version-only should exit 6 like other drift, meaning every repo running this check in CI has had a gate that reports drift and passes anyway; or (b) the documentation is wrong -- a version-only difference genuinely should not fail a build, meaning this is a wording fix scoped to the sentence. checkQuestBlockOnly (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts) already correctly implements QCLI-228s deliberate, tested design: a managed block differing from the installed CLI only in its embedded version number is state version-only and intentionally exits 0 forever, so long as the rest of the content is byte-identical -- QCLI-228 introduced this specifically because gating CI closed on a routine patch/minor version bump alone, with no other content change, was failing builds on drift that was not real. src/application/agents/guides.ts's workspace guide and src/application/command-help.ts's agents entry were both already updated when QCLI-228 landed and correctly describe version-only as a non-failing third state distinct from current/missing/malformed. Only the embedded sentence in questAgentInstructionsFor (the literal text quest agents --update-instructions writes into every consumer's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md) predates QCLI-228 and was never updated to match.
decisions.outcome: Chose (b): documentation was wrong, not the exit code. The embedded CI-hint sentence in questAgentInstructionsFor (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts) now reads: CI should run quest agents --check --require-installed[TARGET]: current instructions, and a version-only difference (only the pinned Quest CLI version number is stale) both exit 0; missing, drifted, or malformed managed instructions exit 6. version-only continues to exit 0 by design (QCLI-228 is not reopened or reversed): a routine patch/minor CLI bump with no other content change in the managed block is not drift, and gating CI on it produces false failures with no actionable fix beyond re-running --update-instructions. This repos own CLAUDE.md managed block was regenerated from the corrected source (quest agents --update-instructions --target claude) so it dogfoods the new sentence and tracker-integrity.yml stays green. test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts gained a test asserting the generated block text explicitly documents the version-only exemption, with a cross-check against checkQuestAgentInstructions's actual behavior for the same input, so a future regression of this exact gap -- text and behavior disagreeing again -- is caught mechanically rather than requiring another externally-filed report. guides.ts and command-help.ts were left unchanged: both already stated the version-only carve-out correctly and needed no correction.
